title: Whole material-transformation cases with role-relative possession and conditional ownership
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED. Complete Institutes II.1.25–28 separates physical transformation, maker contribution, consent, retained individual bodies and legal ownership. The same role-relative own/another expression changes referent with the actor while shared legal rules predict different outcomes.

source_evidence.quote: ## C. JustinianII.1.25–28: Stoffidentität, Beitrag und Einwilligung

source.work: Justinian Institutes II.1.25–28, complete consecutive material-transformation/accession/mixture block
source.historical_date: Sixth-century Institutes, promulgated533; owned Latin is the public digital transcription, whose print-edition genealogy is not established here. Not a newly inspected medieval witness.
source.boundary: Cum ex aliena materia... through ...quale cuiusque frumentum fuerit, immediately before Cum in suo solo...
source.edition_limit: Read in the browser primary-text page; direct HTML request was rejected. This hash therefore owns the copied text below, not the inaccessible HTML response. Source spellings utram and dominoram are retained; section boundaries25–28 are conventional edition locators. No current legal advice.

design.historical_writing_mechanism: Sua/suo/suis are tied to the active maker/actor; aliena/alienis expresses a relation to another owner; tua/tuo and Titii establish a different explicit participant frame. The rule repeats the same conditional constructions across cases while changing arguments, not its meaning per occurrence.
whole_content_model: The introductory ownership question retains both maker and material-owner rival positions and all source examples.
For wholly another material, reducibility to that material selects its owner; irreducibility selects the maker. Metal-vessel and wine/oil/grain/mulsum cases instantiate the contrast.
Partial contribution of the maker’s own material selects the maker, with stated reason of both work and material contribution.
More valuable foreign purple woven into one’s own garment follows accession to the garment, while specified theft/condiction claims remain; maker and thief need not be identical.
Consensual mixtures create common property, whether same or different materials; the described accidental mixtures also do.

Grain mixture is different: consent makes individual grains common, but accidental or unilateral mixture does not, since their individual bodies remain. The herd analogy supplies the same distinction.
If one party retains the whole grain, the other has a proportion-based claim and a judge assesses each party’s grain quality.
design.coupled_consequence: One shared rule cannot infer title merely from final material location, value or maker identity. Reducibility, provenance/contribution and consent interact, with the grain case preserving individual identity. The same final physical mixture can therefore require different ownership and remedy statements.

precise_rivals.rule: The maker always owns the result.
precise_rivals.different_consequence: Fails the wholly foreign reducible metal vessel.

precise_rivals.rule: The original material owner always owns the result.
precise_rivals.different_consequence: Fails the source irreducible transformation and own-plus-foreign contribution cases.

precise_rivals.rule: Every physical mixture makes common title.
precise_rivals.different_consequence: Fails nonconsensual grain where individual corpora persist.
Fails the explicit more-valuable purple accession example.

finite_semantic_restrictions: Maker, original owner, current holder, consenting party and possible thief are distinct roles.
Own/foreign is evaluated relative to the written actor frame, never as fixed names of substances.
Legal title, possession and remedy are distinct predicates; no physical mass-conservation result can substitute for them.
The source’s own physical classifications are held as historical assertions, not replaced by modern chemistry.
unknowns_and_likely_failure: Print-edition ancestry and a medieval witness remain uncollated; source spelling oddities are retained.
No target owner is nominated. A legal register may be an implausible content match for available illustrated passages, and generic argument graphs may not distinguish it without a bounded writer.
No financial or modern legal advice and no claim that historical chemical reversibility statements are experimentally correct.

predecessors.difference: Grant/protection/attestation stages do not provide these material-identity and consent-dependent case contrasts.
Loan separates title and custody but does not supply specification, accession and individual-body mixture countercases; its target is not reused.

predecessors.retained: Linear stock programs and their missing discriminator remain; no stock-identity decoder or alloy number variation is proposed.

design.smallest_future_decision: A whole provisional passage would have to distinguish at least two material cases and a consent/contribution exception under one shared participant grammar. A repeated possession word alone is not the consequence.
